title: Acid-Base Disorders: Thresholds and Compensation Formulas

numbers.context: Normal arterial pH range (<7.35 acidaemia, >7.45 alkalaemia)
Normal serum anion gap (>12 high AG)
Add to AG per 1.0 g/dL albumin below 4.0 g/dL
numbers.source: add 2.5 mEq/L to the observed anion gap for every 1.0 g/dL decrease in serum albumin below 4.0 g/dL

numbers.context: Metabolic alkalosis PaCO2 rise per 1 mEq/L HCO3- above 24 (capped <55 mmHg)
numbers.source: 0.7 mmHg for each 1 mEq/L increase in HCO3- above 24 mEq/L

numbers.context: Respiratory acidosis acute vs chronic HCO3- rise per 10 mmHg PaCO2
Respiratory alkalosis acute vs chronic HCO3- drop per 10 mmHg PaCO2

negations.phrase: compensation never fully normalises pH except possibly in mild chronic respiratory alkalosis
negations.rule: Compensation does not fully normalise pH (except possibly mild chronic respiratory alkalosis)

negations.phrase: Do not assume a normal pH excludes an acid-base disorder
negations.rule: Normal pH with abnormal PaCO2 and HCO3- proves a mixed disorder

negations.phrase: Do not rapidly overcorrect chronic respiratory acidosis with aggressive mechanical ventilation
negations.rule: Avoid rapid overcorrection of chronic hypercapnia (causes post-hypercapnic alkalosis, arrhythmias, seizures)

conditions.phrase: except possibly in mild chronic respiratory alkalosis
conditions.rule: Only possible exception to incomplete pH compensation

conditions.phrase: If measured PaCO2 is higher than Winter's upper limit, a concomitant respiratory acidosis is present
if lower than the lower limit, a concomitant respiratory alkalosis is present

highYield.fact: Normal ABG: pH 7.35-7.45, PaCO2 35-45 mmHg, HCO3- 22-26 mEq/L; AG 8-12 mEq/L
Albumin AG correction: +2.5 mEq/L per 1.0 g/dL albumin below 4.0 g/dL
Winter's formula: Expected PaCO2 = 1.5 x [HCO3-] + 8 +/- 2 mmHg
Respiratory compensation per 10 mmHg PaCO2: acidosis ↑1 acute / ↑3.5-4 chronic; alkalosis ↓2 acute / ↓4-5 chronic
Delta-delta ratio (AG_corr - 12)/(24 - HCO3-): <1 concurrent NAGMA, 1-2 pure HAGMA, >2 concurrent metabolic alkalosis or chronic resp acidosis
Normal pH + abnormal PaCO2 & HCO3- proves mixed disorder; never rapidly overcorrect chronic respiratory acidosis
